instruction: Could you please search for this paper on Google Scholar in Chrome?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for the paper title 'World of Bits: An Open-Domain Platform for Web-Based Agents' on Google Scholar. The evaluator checks if the URL contains both 'https://scholar.google.com/scholar' and 'World+of+Bits' (the search query).
metadata.verification: Verified the paper title from the PDF header. Task maintains similar difficulty - finding the paper on Google Scholar instead of an author's page.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts active Chrome tab URL from accessibility tree using appropriate CSS selectors for Chrome's address bar
Metric logic correctly uses regex pattern matching with re.search() to verify URL contains expected patterns, requiring ALL patterns to match
Expected patterns correctly verify both Google Scholar base URL and search query presence in the URL
URL encoding pattern already handles both '+' and '%20' variations for spaces: (World\+of\+Bits|World%20of%20Bits)
Evaluator semantically verifies complete instruction: search for specific paper on Google Scholar
Postconfig correctly ensures Chrome is running for accessibility tree verification
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts URL string -> metric checks patterns -> returns 1.0 if all match
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Pattern already includes both URL encoding variations (+ and %20), which is excellent for robustness
Pattern focuses on 'World of Bits' key phrase rather than full title - this is pragmatic and sufficient to verify correct search
No critical fixes needed - evaluator is semantically sound and handles edge cases well
